programme: RBPJ (CSL), the obligate transcriptional effector of canonical Notch, driving its own target genes (HES1, HEY1, HEY2, NOTCH1, NOTCH3, DLK1) sits alongside a cluster of lineage-fate/oncofetal transcription factors — PLAG1 (activates the fetal growth driver IGF2), HOXD9 (posterior HOX reactivation), GCM1 and NFIA (glial/progenitor specification factors), CEBPG (a C/EBP-family bZIP that can antagonize CEBPA-driven terminal differentiation), and HLX (visceral-endoderm/hematopoietic progenitor homeobox). Together these describe a fate-maintenance module that keeps cells in, or pushes them back toward, a progenitor-like/oncofetal transcriptional state rather than a terminally differentiated one.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's-affected brain, reactive/disease-associated astrocytes and microglia re-express developmental and progenitor-lineage programs rather than staying in their mature state; RBPJ/Notch(HES1/HEY) output together with the glial-specification factors GCM1 and NFIA would be the regulators running that shift, with NFIA independently linked to AD by GWAS and spatial transcriptomics.
role_in_b: In hepatocellular/liver cancer, the same kind of module drives dedifferentiation of hepatocytes toward a fetal, hepatoblast/progenitor-like state: PLAG1 reactivating IGF2 is a textbook oncofetal driver, RBPJ/Notch output (HES1/HEY/DLK1) marks the hepatic progenitor-versus-hepatocyte fate switch exploited by tumors, HOXD9 is reactivated in HCC tissue, and CEBPG opposes CEBPA-driven hepatocyte maturation.
shared_axis: Both diseases would recruit the same progenitor/fate-maintenance module — RBPJ-driven Notch output plus PLAG1, HOXD9, GCM1, NFIA, CEBPG and HLX — to move differentiated cells backward along a developmental axis: hepatocytes toward a fetal/progenitor state in liver cancer, and neurons/glia toward a reactive, developmentally-primed state in Alzheimer's.
reasoning: The module is nameable and internally consistent — RBPJ's target list is canonical Notch/CSL output, and the flanking factors are established progenitor/oncofetal regulators — and NFIA and HOXD9 are each independently placed in one of the two diseases by retrieved papers, satisfying part of the bar for moderate support. But no retrieved paper discusses the module as a whole or any connection between Alzheimer's Disease and Liver Cancer specifically, and NOTCH1/SOX10 were separately flagged as tissue-generic, so the Notch component of this story may partly reflect biology generic to brain and liver rather than something specific to this disease pair.
support: 38751862 places HOXD9 in a hepatocellular-carcinoma macrophage-polarization prognostic model (Liver_Cancer); 33640202 is a GWAS linking NFIA to brain atrophy in Alzheimer's Disease; 39543008 places NFIA in spatial transcriptomic architecture of Alzheimer's Disease tissue; 41935644 and 41317176 discuss IRF7 in Alzheimer's Disease contexts (interferon/hippocampal pathway), adjacent to but not confirmed as part of this specific module; 40467545 and 40979532 mention FOXP2 in Alzheimer's Disease amyloid/treatment studies (placement only, no mechanism). No paper was found discussing RBPJ, PLAG1, GCM1, CEBPG, or HLX in either disease, and none connects the two diseases through this axis.
how_to_falsify: In matched HCC tumor vs adjacent-liver tissue and AD-affected vs unaffected brain tissue, test whether RBPJ occupancy/target induction (HES1, HEY1, HEY2, DLK1) co-occurs with induction of PLAG1, HOXD9, GCM1, NFIA and CEBPG in the specific dedifferentiating/reactive cell populations (progenitor-like hepatocytes in HCC; disease-associated astrocyte/microglia states in AD), compared to unrelated tissue-pair controls that also carry generic Notch/progenitor biology. If co-induction is absent, or no more specific to this pair than to arbitrary tissue pairs, the account fails.
caveats: Brain|liver pairing spans 80 patient-group comparisons but only 3 independent cohort pairs, limiting true replication; NOTCH1 and SOX10 were removed as tissue-generic, so the Notch/glial-identity signal in general is common to both tissues and RBPJ should be read as one specific effector riding an otherwise generic pathway, not proof of a disease-specific rewiring; the single-view exclusions (TEF, KCNIP3, NFATC3, MRTFA, PURB, PLAGL2, STAT6, NKX2-2, NACC1, SMAD9) rule out circadian/metabolic/single-cohort stories being the real driver; most of the carrying factors (PLAG1, GCM1, CEBPG, HLX, RBPJ itself) have zero disease-specific literature retrieved or explicitly off-topic hits, so this account leans on canonical pathway knowledge more than on the retrieved record for this particular pair.
